A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DADO research, with matching authors, objectives, algorithm, and theoretical development. Text extraction and visual inspection cover all 27 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including their appendices, without material comparison gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.6 report original synthetic optimization experiments, evaluations on seven protein datasets, sampling-budget ablations, and a GB1 decomposition study.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.9 report original optimization experiments, additional baseline comparisons, graph-robustness studies, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: DADO retains the same junction-tree factorization, conditional sampling, distributional value functions, message passing, and per-factor weighted maximum-likelihood updates. Algorithm 1 and the corresponding derivations are substantively unchanged. FDA and PPO are added comparison methods, not new DADO components.

E1.justification: v2 extends synthetic task coverage to length L=400 and alphabets D=50 and D=100, testing larger discrete design spaces. All seven protein datasets remain. Gcn4 replacing GB1 in the main figure is a change in emphasis, since both appeared in v1 and remain evaluated in v2.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares DADO with a naive EDA. v2 adds FDA and a PPO-style EDA to the retained main synthetic and protein comparisons. FDA uses DADO's factorization, providing a substantive control for message passing. The new predictor-robustness experiments also include an undecomposed neural-network comparator labeled Naive NN.

E3.justification: Reported protein initialization changes from the 1,000 lowest assay-label sequences to the 1,000 lowest-f(x) sequences, and hyperparameter sweeps are now broadened when optima reach their boundaries. New protocols include reusing L=200 hyperparameters at L=400 and training on bottom-half assay labels against unchanged holdouts. Most significance evaluations now target final-iteration performance instead of trajectory AUC.

E4.justification: v2 adds a message-passing control through FDA, larger-length/alphabet analyses, runtime analysis, and five-protein studies of contact thresholds and random edge perturbations, including bottom-half-label training. The original GB1 threshold case study survives as Figure A6. However, v1's synthetic K=100 versus 1000 and seven-protein K=100 versus 1000 sampling-budget ablations are removed.

E5.justification: The 20-seed, 95% confidence-interval, paired two-sided t-test framework remains. Most tests change from AUC to final-iteration means, and Figures 2–3 compare against the strongest baseline. New graph-mutation studies report ten repetitions and display replicate variability. The retained GB1 case study still uses its original AUC tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds FDA/PPO results, larger synthetic-design results, robustness correlations, and runtime measurements, while removing sampling-budget results. FDA is competitive with DADO on GB1 and exceeds it on ynzC and CreiLOV in Figure A4. Existing protein trajectories and p-values also change. Revised initialization and statistical comparisons prevent treating these revisions as uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The decomposition definitions, EDA derivation, distributional-value lower-bound reasoning, and maximum-entropy derivation are retained. v1 Appendices A.3–A.4 correspond to v2 A.4–A.5. The new A.3 largely relocates the earlier algorithmic explanation; equation renumbering and compressed notation do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains distributional optimization that exploits arbitrary junction-tree decomposability through message passing. v2 adds an explicit contribution claiming predictor accuracy is robust to decomposition modifications and broadens the empirical comparison claims to multiple baselines. These extend the supporting claims without redefining the research contribution.

C2.justification: v2 introduces explanations involving noisy value estimates in large junction-tree nodes, FDA's competitiveness, and reduced overfitting from stronger decomposition under shifted training data. It removes v1's explicit Gcn4 caveat about intrinsic disorder and multiple conformations, instead emphasizing limited, dispersed data. These materially revise the account of applicability, failure mechanisms, and robustness.

D1.justification: v2 documents the FDA/PPO implementations, including PPO clipping at 0.2, clarifies atom-based contact construction, and adds single-GPU runtime and memory/parallel-execution information. Most architecture, optimizer, and predictor-training details in A.8 were already in v1 Section 4, although the within-node decoding and overlapping-variable explanation is shortened. The public code-access statement remains.

R1.justification: FDA and PPO were already cited in v1; v2 expands their discussion as controls for factorization and update stabilization. The Design-Bench reference by Trabucco et al. (2022) disappears with the continuous-design future-work discussion. The broader positioning relative to EDAs, reinforcement learning, and Bayesian optimization is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, intuitive method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively edited and condensed. Detailed algorithm sketches move to A.3, implementation material moves to A.8, and the appendix is reorganized into dedicated baseline, implementation, and analysis sections. Terminology, headings, affiliations, and conference formatting also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds the extensive protein-structure/contact-graph/junction-tree Figure A1, robustness figures, and runtime Table 1. Main comparison plots gain FDA/PPO curves and revised legends. Protein plots introduce the -log(c-f(x)) scale, with ordinary-scale counterparts retained in the appendix, and the main protein panels are reordered and reselected. The document is comprehensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked an evaluated control separating factorization from message passing. v2's matched FDA comparison addresses that central attribution gap, while robustness studies and runtime measurements substantially strengthen assessment of practical applicability and reveal cases favoring FDA. Removing sampling-budget ablations, dropping the explicit Gcn4 structural caveat, and emphasizing endpoint tests lose useful information, but the new controls and boundary analyses provide a clear, substantial net improvement.
